players.product: medium-voltage switchgear, power control rooms / electrical houses and Remsdaq automation controllers for data-center utility connection (38 kV) and behind-the-meter on-site generation power islands

quarterly_data.signal: Fiscal Q1 2026 results (CFO Mike Metcalf): net revenue $251 million vs $241 million, 4% higher YoY (CEO Brett Cope notes the first fiscal quarter 'typically exhibits some level of seasonal disruptions associated with fewer working days'). Gross profit up $12 million to $71 million; gross margin 28.4%, 'an improvement of 380 basis points year-over-year', driven by strong project execution and a higher level of project closeouts (sequentially lower by 300 basis points on seasonal softness). SG&A $25.2 million (10% of revenue). Net income $41.4 million or $3.40 per diluted share, a 19% increase vs $34.8 million or $2.86. By market: utility revenue higher by 35%, oil and gas +2%, petrochemical lower by 31% (completion of a large project booked in fiscal 2023 plus softer activity), commercial and other industrial 8% lower on project timing, light rail traction power 5% higher. Domestic revenues lower by 1% to $195 million; international revenues up 29% to $44 million on projects in the Middle East and Africa, Asia Pacific and Europe.
quarterly_data.figure: net revenue $251 million (4% higher); gross margin 28.4% (+380 basis points); net income $41.4 million, $3.40 per diluted share; utility revenue higher by 35%

quarterly_data.signal: Orders and backlog: Q1 new orders $439 million, 63% higher than a year ago and 'the highest quarterly total in over 2 years', with activity 'widespread across oil and gas, specifically LNG, data centers and the electric utilities markets'; book-to-bill 1.7x. Orders included a mega order for a large domestic LNG project on the U.S. Gulf Coast valued at greater than $100 million; Cope expects LNG activity to continue in 2026 and a wave of LNG project development over the next 3 to 5 years. Backlog $1.6 billion, 'the highest in Powell's history', 14% sequential growth ($191 million higher sequentially) and $219 million higher YoY; oil and gas and utility each roughly 30% of backlog, and electric utility plus commercial and other industrial 'now account for the majority of our backlog for the first time ever'. Project visibility 'now extends into our fiscal 2028'; Cope calls the backlog 'very durable'.
quarterly_data.figure: orders $439 million (63% higher); book-to-bill 1.7x; record backlog $1.6 billion (14% sequential growth, $219 million higher YoY); LNG mega order greater than $100 million

quarterly_data.signal: DATA-CENTER ORDERS AT RECORD SHARE: Metcalf says Q1 data center orders 'totaled more than $100 million', booked in the commercial and other industrial sector, including 'a notable mega order for electrical distribution equipment' valued at approximately $75 million 'that will be deployed at a single data center' - Cope calls it 'our first mega project order for a single data center'. Commercial and other industrial accounted for 'nearly 1/2 of the order total' and now comprises 22% of backlog, with data centers roughly 15% of total backlog, 'both of which are record levels for Powell'. Cope cites 'increasing levels of interest among a growing list of data center customers', driven by rising power demand and the desire to expedite construction timelines, and 'our first orders in the United States' for products of Remsdaq Limited (U.K.).
quarterly_data.figure: data center orders more than $100 million; first single-data-center mega order approximately $75 million; commercial and other industrial 22% of backlog, data centers roughly 15% (both record levels)

quarterly_data.signal: DATA-CENTER VOLTAGE MIX AND LEAD TIMES: asked about component lead times, Cope says data-center power levels have increased, whether 'coming off utility or if they're doing GTG, self-generation on site or any kind of multifuel, there's a lot going into the 38 kV line, and that is ramping quickly' - a product that 'fits Powell really well'. At the 5 and 15 levels 'they're not as robust. We actually have capacity': newer designs with '90 or 100 or 150-megawatt data halls' can still be served at '35 to 40 weeks on gear, which is very competitive in the market' for 15 kb [kV] gear, which 'will benefit the back half of this year and into the early part of '27'. Powell is 'driving future capacity for those higher levels that are really under demand' and phasing deliveries with clients.
quarterly_data.figure: 38 kV line ramping quickly; capacity available at the 5 and 15 levels; 35 to 40 weeks on gear for 15 kb [kV]

quarterly_data.signal: CAPACITY ADDITIONS: Powell added 'a 50,000 lease square foot lease facility, which we're just taking ownership now' to support product-line flow and store the inventory needed for repetitive data-center builds ('a lot of design one, build many'), is evaluating additional facilities, and is 'considering right now something on the order of another $100 million type facility' - 'We've not pulled the trigger on that', with active Board discussions. Cope says the new capacity could support revenue growth where 'I think double digits is possible'. Other measures: broader supply-base collaboration to ramp supply and improve cycle times, and rebalancing products across North American facilities; the Jacintoport expansion is on schedule for completion in the second half of fiscal 2026, aimed mainly at oil and gas / LNG. The 50,000 square foot breaker-plant investment in Houston last year means Powell is 'already prepped' for some low-voltage content. Constraint: engineering needs on the fixed side, challenged by growth in the commercial segment, which Cope expects to solve 'in the next 90 days or so'.
quarterly_data.figure: 50,000 lease square foot lease facility; considering another $100 million type facility; Jacintoport expansion completion in the second half of fiscal 2026

quarterly_data.signal: PRODUCT SCOPE WIDENING IN DATA CENTERS: Cope says the data center / commercial market 'opened the door to allow us to get that technology in quicker than we anticipated into the U.S. market' for Remsdaq (acquired last summer), applying its protective and control logic to data-center power trains, and 'We just took our first order for a high-voltage control protection substation the utility connect ... which would be a new space for Powell', enabled by Remsdaq; the business 'is accretive to margin significantly'. Inside the data center, low-voltage content on current AC designs 'will be a pretty chunky add', and Powell is also involved in 'the future DC designs' ('it will be a step change'). Data-center service: quotes are out for constructability and timing support, but 'We haven't closed anything yet'.

MARGIN FRAMEWORK AND BACKLOG CONVERSION: Metcalf says trailing-12-month reported margins are 'running about 30%' including 'approximately 175 basis points of project closeout gains', so 'maintaining a base level margin in the upper 20s while continuing to drive for 150 to 200 basis point upside resulting from favorable closeouts is a reasonable assumption'. Of the $1.6 billion backlog, 'roughly 60% of that is convertible over the next 12 months' ($933 million in the 10-Q), plus book-and-bill running at a '$65 million to $70 million cadence every quarter'. Pricing: 'No real change', holding steady in all verticals; Cope sees 'potential upside' on repetitive data-center product builds as efficiency improves. Input costs: copper is hedged to some extent and increases are rolled into pricing models; engineered components (HVAC, fire systems) are locked in at contract signing. Metcalf is 'optimistic that we can sustain the quantity and the quality of our backlog throughout fiscal 2026'.
quarterly_data.figure: base margin in the upper 20s plus 150 to 200 basis point closeout upside; roughly 60% of the $1.6 billion backlog convertible over the next 12 months ($933 million); book-and-bill $65 million to $70 million every quarter

quarterly_data.signal: CUSTOMERS SEEKING TO LOCK CAPACITY: asked whether customers are buying just to get in line, Cope says 'are people talking to us and others about reservations and locking capacity, yes, those conversations are happening', a 'future concern that's on our radar' but 'not currently in the backlog'. The number of customers holding strategic discussions 'is increasing', engagements are 'going out further in time', and for data centers built in phases 'the size of the data center potential that could be added on to it is definitely part of the conversation'; Powell screens for clients that align with it. Asked by an analyst whether book-to-bill can stay above 1 over the next two years, Cope says 'I think it's reasonable'.

Balance sheet and capital deployment: Q1 operating cash flow $43.6 million; PP&E investment $2 million (capacity and productivity); cash and short-term investments $501 million at December 31, 2025 vs $476 million at September 30, 2025, no debt. Metcalf: 'roughly 40% to 50% of that balance will be deployed at some point in the future to that $1.6 billion backlog number', leaving 'probably $200 million to $225 million' of free cash for capital deployment such as capacity. Cope says Powell is 'not slowing down on the M&A side' after Remsdaq, and a stock split is under active Board discussion as an equity tool for employees.
quarterly_data.figure: cash and short-term investments $501 million, no debt; operating cash flow $43.6 million; $200 million to $225 million free cash for capital deployment
